verdict.rationale: Pipedream's docs list an HTTP / Webhook trigger as a first-party workflow trigger type. A community thread confirms HTTP triggers run with execution limits (100kb max body size, 10 req/s, 10s per execution). The evidence never shows the trigger creating a custom endpoint URL, or the incoming request payload reaching the workflow run, so the story is only partly evidenced. missing for 10: documentation of a generated or custom webhook URL, documentation of how the HTTP request payload/body/headers are passed into the workflow run, in-depth first-party docs on the HTTP trigger, hands-on corroboration of end-to-end webhook-triggered runs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a custom webhook URL that receives external HTTP requests and starts a workflow run with the payload

citations.quote: Today, we support the following triggers: ... HTTP / Webhook ... Schedule ... Email ... RSS
Then you can select a specific test event and manually trigger your workflow with that event data by clicking Send Test Event.
100kb max body-size, rate-limit at 10 req/s, 10s per execution for HTTP triggers
